tasks.short: Install hardware or program microprocessor-based instrumentation systems

steps.what: Read actual equipment identity, hardware revision, approved installation instructions and instrumentation software compatibility using native asset and revision views
inputs: Actual equipment identification and current manufacturer instructions
outputs: Verified installation and compatibility context

steps.what: Prepare the actual hardware connections or instrumentation program and configuration for the identified microprocessor system, checking addresses, versions and rollback requirements
inputs: Actual system and verified technical requirements
outputs: Prepared hardware arrangement or actual program and configuration

steps.what: Check current physical isolation, actual equipment state, permitted work scope and the exact prepared installation or program before deciding whether the actual operation may proceed
inputs: Actual current equipment state and s2 exact prepared hardware or program
outputs: Current actual installation readiness decision for the identified equipment and configuration

steps.what: Perform the exact permitted hardware installation or instrumentation program load on the actual microprocessor system
inputs: Actual equipment and exact prepared configuration with current s3 operational readiness
outputs: Actually installed hardware or loaded instrumentation program

steps.what: Test actual installed functions against the applicable instructions and identify failures before any separate return-to-service process
inputs: Actually installed equipment or loaded program and actual test instruments
outputs: Observed functional test results and unresolved faults

steps.what: Write the actual required equipment entry identifying installed versions, hardware changes and observed test outcomes after the work
inputs: Actual completed installation and observed test results
outputs: Accurate equipment work entry

steps.what: Save the completed entry in the same equipment work record
inputs: Completed actual work entry
outputs: Stored work entry

tasks.design: Configure {OPS_SYSTEM} asset and revision views to retrieve actual installation context from {DOCS}. The technician prepares the real configuration in {OTHER}, the manufacturer programming and test tools, checks current operational readiness, performs installation and records actual test results.
tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment identity and compatible instructions can require repeated navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing asset and revision filters can expose the actual corresponding documents.
tasks.still_hard: Hardware compatibility, physical installation and real functional tests remain equipment-specific work.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an unsafe or incompatible installation and stop it.

ambition.what: Improve source access for existing installation work.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: asset and revision views can locate existing equipment instructions without installing or validating hardware or software.

assumptions: Illustrative actual installation episode, not a measured baseline or the whole mix of hardware and programming work. Manufacturer and engineering staff produce existing instructions; s1 includes actual equipment identification and compatibility reading, s2 counts real configuration preparation. No clean program or test feed is free.

S3 is the actual technician's current physical and operational readiness decision, not approval of authored paperwork or an ordinary save. It applies only within actual delegated operating authority. The exact prepared configuration exists first; changes to it, equipment state or work scope void a1 and require fresh readiness. Separate permit or engineering authority requirements must follow the real process and are not invented as completed.

S4 is one actual hardware installation or software-load action. If the episode has multiple separately authorised commits, model each actual action and gate rather than treating this as blanket permission. No separate return-to-service release is hidden in testing or saving.

The actual required post-work entry is separate from physical work. Its ordinary same-system save is negligible, minimum integer share 1 fully retained, ungated and carries no saving. Try native views first; existing use yields no new benefit. Shares are independent of prompt time priors.
unknowns: Are actual hardware revisions indexed against the right instructions?
Which installation and load permissions apply to the specific equipment?
research_questions: Observe one actual installation and measure document navigation separately from preparation, readiness, physical work, tests and record writing.

already_counted.description: Verified context, actual preparation, readiness, installation, test and work entry including save remain in s1-s7.

incremental.description: Repair asset-to-instruction links beyond retained per-installation checks.

approvals.approved_version: Exact hardware arrangement or program/configuration prepared in s2 for the identified equipment under the current physical state and permitted scope checked in s3; any change voids readiness

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High: 15*.10=1.5 source-navigation points less .5 extra link upkeep =1. Low: hardware revision labels do not resolve to indexed compatible instructions, so all 15 source points remain manual and no unhelpful configuration or upkeep is introduced. Preparation, actual readiness, installation, tests, entry and ordinary save remain fully retained. Unmeasured compatibility-specific scenarios.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read technical drawings and orders to determine assembly methods and sequence

steps.what: Retrieve actual released blueprints, schematics, diagrams and technical orders with the native drawing register's assembly and revision filters
inputs: Actual assembly identity and existing drawing register
outputs: Identified original technical drawings and current revision context

steps.what: Read the original drawings and technical orders, interpret interfaces, tolerances, dependencies and actual assembly constraints
inputs: Actual drawings, schematics and technical orders
outputs: Understood assembly requirements and unresolved technical questions

steps.what: Determine the actual assembly method and sequence and write the existing working sequence note, inserting checked drawing references using native linked fields
inputs: Actual interpreted requirements and checked drawing identifiers
outputs: Actual working assembly sequence with verified drawing references

steps.what: Save the working sequence note in its existing document system
inputs: Completed working assembly sequence
outputs: Stored working sequence

tasks.design: Use {OPS_SYSTEM} drawing-register filters to find actual assembly documents and {DOCS} linked reference fields in the existing working note. The technician reads the original technical content and determines the assembly sequence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drawing retrieval and repeated revision reference entry interrupt technical interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native assembly and revision filters and document reference fields can reduce that clerical work.
tasks.still_hard: Interfaces, tolerances and safe sequencing require technical interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise contradictory drawings and ask for engineering clarification.

ambition.what: Support technical reading without generating an unverified assembly method.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: drawing registers can filter identifiers and revisions and document tools can reuse checked references; interpreting assembly dependencies remains technical work.

assumptions: Representative technical-reading episode that actually produces a working sequence note. No additional formal report or assembly action is invented. Actual engineering authors produce drawings; s1 counts identification and retrieval, s2 original reading, s3 sequence reasoning, writing and reference checking.
S3's reduction covers only native insertion of checked references; it does not reduce assembly reasoning. If reference links are already native and used, their new benefit is zero.

This task ends with a working sequence, not a released production instruction, purchase, message or equipment operation. Actual formal instruction release would require its real independent final-version authority and separate gated action.

The ordinary same-system save is minimum integer share 1 representing negligible actual time, fully retained and ungated. No author self-approval. Shares are task-specific illustrative effort rather than prompt-prior allocations.
unknowns: Does the drawing register have reliable assembly and revision metadata?
Is the working sequence actually written today and are its references linked already?
research_questions: Observe actual technical reading and separate retrieval, interpretation and existing note production.

already_counted.description: Actual retrieval checking, original drawing interpretation, assembly sequence writing and ordinary save remain in s1-s4.

incremental.description: Maintain drawing-reference links and register filters beyond retained case checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High: 20*.25+29*.10=7.9 gross less 2 upkeep =5.9. Low: assembly aliases and revision labels are not consistently indexed, so all 20 retrieval points remain, while individually verified drawing references can still populate the working note and save 2.9; 2.9-2=.9. All original reading and sequence reasoning remains. This is a drawing-register metadata case, unmeasured.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Modify, maintain or repair electromechanical components and equipment

steps.what: Read actual fault history and applicable component instructions using existing equipment and fault-code views
inputs: Actual work request, equipment identity and existing technical history
outputs: Verified maintenance context

steps.what: Inspect and test actual electrical, electronic or mechanical components, diagnose the fault and determine the permitted maintenance or repair method
inputs: Actual equipment and physical diagnostic measurements
outputs: Actual diagnosis and identified repair method

steps.what: Check actual current isolation, equipment state, tools, parts and work authority before deciding whether the exact proposed repair may proceed
inputs: Actual current worksite conditions and s2 exact repair method
outputs: Current actual readiness decision for the specified physical repair

steps.what: Carry out the exact permitted physical modification, maintenance or repair on the actual identified component
inputs: Actual component, tools, parts and valid current s3 readiness
outputs: Actually maintained or repaired component

steps.what: Test the repaired component's actual functioning and identify any remaining faults
inputs: Actually repaired component and real test instruments
outputs: Actual observed functional results and remaining defects

steps.what: Write the actual required maintenance entry describing work performed, parts used, measured results and remaining faults
inputs: Actual completed repair and real test results
outputs: Accurate actual maintenance entry

steps.what: Save the entry in the same maintenance record
inputs: Completed maintenance entry
outputs: Stored maintenance entry

tasks.design: Use {OPS_SYSTEM} history filters to locate actual equipment context, with instructions in {DOCS}. The technician diagnoses, checks current physical readiness, repairs and tests the real component using {OTHER}, the actual instruments and maintenance tools, then writes the required entry.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the matching equipment history can require navigation before physical diagnosis.
tasks.enabler_now: Native asset and fault-code views can expose existing history.
tasks.still_hard: Actual faults and repair outcomes require measurements and physical work.
tasks.human_edge: Detect conditions that make the planned repair inappropriate and stop.

ambition.what: Reduce source navigation within real maintenance work.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: asset history filters reduce information navigation but do not diagnose, repair or test physical components.

assumptions: Actual existing work request and prior maintenance authors supply source history; s1 reads it, s2 captures real measurements and diagnoses the fault. No clean sensor feed or free prepared diagnosis is assumed. Required record writing is split from physical maintenance in s6 rather than declaring the task wholly manual.

S3 is an actual immediate physical readiness decision within the technician's real delegated work scope, not self-approval of a written record. Exact proposed work exists first. Changes to method, isolation, conditions or equipment invalidate a1. Actual additional permit authorities must be represented if required and are not deemed satisfied here.

The representative episode has one physical repair action; additional separately controlled actions require their own current readiness. A return-to-service release, engineering change release, parts purchase or written notification is not hidden in testing or saving.

Try existing views first; if already used there is no new runtime benefit. Save share 1 is minimum integer representation of negligible actual time, fully retained, ungated and without saving. Shares are illustrative and independent of prompt time priors.
unknowns: Are fault codes and component identities consistent across the maintenance history?
Which actual operational permissions apply to the proposed repair?
research_questions: Observe diagnosis, actual repair, functional test and required entry separately from history navigation.

already_counted.description: Actual history checking, diagnosis, readiness, physical repair, functional test and record writing including save remain in s1-s7.

incremental.description: Repair fault-view links beyond retained per-job checking.

approvals.approved_version: Exact repair method determined in s2 for the actual component under the current isolation, physical conditions and delegated scope checked in s3; changes void readiness

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High: 10*.10=1 history-navigation point less .3 extra upkeep =.7. Low: inconsistent fault codes prevent useful history filtering and actual component identity must be traced manually, retaining all 10 source points; no new view or upkeep is introduced. Diagnosis25, readiness10, repair40, test10, entry4 and save1 remain fully retained. An equipment-history comparability case, not an administrative baseline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Produce CAD drawings and graphics for electromechanical design

steps.what: Read actual design requirements and component models, verify dimensions, units, CAD layers and source revisions and map the required output views and drawing metadata
inputs: Actual engineering requirements, component models and drawing standards
outputs: Verified model inputs, view choices and explicit title-field mapping

steps.what: Create the actual electrical, electronic or mechanical design geometry and connections and choose the necessary dimensions, annotations and representations
inputs: Actual verified requirements and component context
outputs: Actual design geometry, connections and chosen annotations

steps.what: Generate the explicitly selected drawing views from the actual design model with fixed projection, scale and visible-layer settings
inputs: S2 actual design model and s1 explicit output-view settings
outputs: Regenerated drawing views and incompatible-layer exceptions

steps.what: Populate the actual drawing's title block, component identifiers and revision fields from the explicitly verified source mapping
inputs: S1 verified metadata mapping and actual drawing views
outputs: Drawing with mapped metadata and missing-field exceptions

steps.what: Check the complete drawing against original requirements, actual geometry, connections, dimensions, layers, references and revision fields and correct errors manually
inputs: Complete generated drawing and original design requirements
outputs: Technically checked actual working drawing

steps.what: Save the working drawing in the same native CAD document
inputs: Checked actual working drawing
outputs: Stored working CAD drawing

tasks.design: Use {OTHER}, the existing electromechanical CAD application, to generate explicitly selected views and mapped title fields after the technician creates and verifies the actual design. Keep geometry choices, annotation meaning and complete technical checking with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Where views and title fields are rebuilt manually, actual design changes require repeated drafting operations.
tasks.enabler_now: Native associative views and mapped drawing fields can perform explicit repetitive drafting deterministically.
tasks.still_hard: Model compatibility and technical meaning require real engineering checks.
tasks.human_edge: Choose correct geometry and representations and recognise a misleading drawing.

ambition.what: Reduce demonstrated repetitive CAD production without claiming automatic electromechanical design.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: CAD systems can regenerate selected model views and populate mapped drawing fields; design and technical checking remain human responsibilities.

assumptions: Conditional on observing actual manual view rebuilding and field entry today. If native associativity and title fields already do this, no new gain; do not invent a manual baseline. Try native settings before any extension.

Engineering authors produce requirements and actual component models. S1 counts source retrieval, dimension and unit checks, layer compatibility and field mapping; s2 counts actual design production. No clean model or free upstream capture is assumed. Missing or incompatible geometry remains manual.

S3 and s4 are explicit separate deterministic actions; no model is needed to choose engineering geometry. S5 retains all technical checking and exception correction. Incremental mapping upkeep is deducted once, not again from already retained source work.

Task ends with a working CAD drawing. No production release, engineering-change commit, external send or manufacturing action is hidden in the save; those require their actual independent final-version authority and distinct gated action if part of a real workflow.

The ordinary same-system save is negligible, minimum integer share 1 fully retained and ungated, with no self-approval or saving. All shares are illustrative task effort independent of prompt time priors.
unknowns: Which actual views are rebuilt manually rather than associatively?
Do component layers and title-field metadata survive the native drawing pipeline?
research_questions: Observe a real drawing revision and distinguish design choices, source preparation, repetitive view and field operations and complete checking.

already_counted.description: Source verification and mapping, actual design choices, complete drawing checking and ordinary save remain in s1, s2, s5 and s6.

incremental.description: Maintain view and title-field mappings and sample regeneration errors beyond retained per-drawing source and technical checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High: actual manual views20 plus title fields15 become deterministic =35 gross less 4 upkeep =31. Low: incompatible component layers require all 20 view points to remain manual and 4 of the 15 title-field points require manual metadata repair; only 11 title-field points save, less 4 upkeep =7. Source20, design25, complete check19 and save1 remain in both cases. These are layer-compatibility and output-metadata scenarios; native features already in use yield zero new benefit instead.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

Actual operational authorities retain equipment permissions and separate release decisions
skills_to_grow: Map CAD views and output metadata explicitly
Separate physical readiness, ordinary record saves and formal release actions
